description: Use this when the user wants to CANCEL an engagement request (an introduction) they already raised and that is still waiting on the other side. Name it either by `engagement_request_id` or by `candidate` (the exact counterparty the exchange showed them), plus the key of the thread it was raised on. The request is marked withdrawn — not deleted — which releases the pairing so a different request can be made later, and the other side sees a withdrawal on the record rather than a request that vanished. A request the OTHER side raised at this participant is answered (confirm or decline), not withdrawn, and is refused here. The call is staged: a dry run sends nothing, and the confirmed call is bound to the exact payload that dry run returned. Call once with dry_run=true to get the exact payload and a confirmation_token; call again with the same arguments plus that token to send. A token that does not match the payload is refused and nothing is sent.

candidate.description: OR the exact counterparty name the request was raised against. Provide this or engagement_request_id — never guessed.

confirmation_token.description: The token from the dry run, for the confirmed withdrawal.

dry_run.description: true returns the exact withdrawal and a confirmation_token, and withdraws nothing.

engagement_request_id.description: The id of the live request to withdraw, as get_exchange_answer reports it under state.pairings[].pending_request.

key.description: The msgid (or answer_key) of the thread the engagement request was raised on.

reason.description: Optional reason in the user's own words, recorded with the withdrawal.

request_id.description: Your own idempotency key for this withdrawal; quote it as the receipt.

name: withdraw_engagement
title: Withdraw an engagement request you raised
